title: LeverageBrief
description: Pre-research intellectual contract for an Asymmetric episode. Locks the hidden mechanism, control surface, cost transfer chain, beneficiaries, accountability gap, and advertiser safety posture before scripting begins.

episode_id.description: Unique slug identifying this episode, e.g. 'ai-datacenter-cost-transfer-p001'.

public_story.description: The consensus narrative most people believe. State it fairly and without mockery.

hidden_mechanism.description: How the system actually works beneath the public story. Must be provable with primary sources.

control_surface.description: The specific mechanism, clause, rule, rate schedule, or policy that concentrates control. Must be nameable and documentable.

dependency.description: Who depends on the control surface and has no structural alternative. Explain why exit is not available.

cost_transfer.description: Ordered list of cost transfer steps. Each step names who absorbs what cost through what mechanism.

mechanism.description: The structural mechanism by which the cost is transferred (e.g. 'rate case inclusion', 'tax incentive', 'subsidy agreement').

estimated_magnitude.description: Estimated magnitude of the cost transfer. Use 'unknown' if not yet established; do not leave blank.

beneficiaries.description: Entities that capture value from the mechanism. Each entry names the beneficiary and the capture mechanism.

capture_mechanism.description: How this entity captures value (e.g. 'subsidized construction cost', 'monopoly toll', 'asset ownership with socialized risk').

accountability_gap.description: Why the mechanism escapes consequence. Name the structural gap: regulatory capture, jurisdictional void, enforcement lapse, sunsetted disclosure requirement, etc.

viewer_takeaway.description: The single reusable mental model the viewer carries out. One sentence.

leverage_takeaway.description: The structured operator-level takeaway. Gives the viewer a framework to apply in adjacent situations.

what_to_watch_for.description: Signals in adjacent systems that indicate the same mechanism is operating.

questions_to_ask.description: Specific questions an operator should ask when they see these signals.

documents_to_find.description: Specific document types that expose the mechanism (rate filings, subsidy agreements, platform policies, etc.). May be empty if no specific document type applies.

safe_action_language.description: Language describing what viewers can do with this knowledge. Must be informational, lawful, non-harassing, and non-partisan.

advertiser_safety_posture.description: Declares the advertiser safety posture for this episode. Governs language discipline throughout production.

risk_level.description: low = pure structural analysis; medium = named entities with documented behavior; high = named individuals or implied misconduct.

language_approved.description: Approved terms for this episode's language posture. Must include at least one term from the advertiser safety approved list.

language_forbidden.description: Forbidden terms specific to this episode, in addition to the channel-wide forbidden list.

claim_source_required.description: Every factual claim must map to a primary source before scripting. Always true.
